# Blinkql

> Blinkql is an open-source SQL workbench that runs entirely in the browser, for files too big for a spreadsheet and too sensitive to upload: CSV, Parquet and JSON exports of 1–2 million rows, and Excel workbooks. Queries run locally, and files never leave the user's computer. Version 1.1 is out; it was built in the open across nine milestones.

The workbench is at https://blinkql.karthik.nz/app/. Licensed under MIT.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/Karthik-beta/Blinkql/blob/main/README.md): what Blinkql does and how to start
- [Roadmap and milestones](https://github.com/Karthik-beta/Blinkql/wiki/Roadmap-and-Milestones): the nine milestones from M0 to version 1.1
- [Use cases](https://github.com/Karthik-beta/Blinkql/wiki/Use-Cases): who it's for, with examples from factories and operations
- [Privacy and security](https://github.com/Karthik-beta/Blinkql/wiki/Privacy-and-Security): why no data leaves the browser
- [Architecture](https://github.com/Karthik-beta/Blinkql/wiki/Architecture): how the browser-based engine fits together
